sources.entry: annoy - Approximate Nearest Neighbors in C++/Python optimized for memory usage.

summary.one_liner: Annoy is a C++ library with Python bindings for approximate nearest neighbor search, building file-based indexes that can be memory-mapped and shared across processes.
summary.what_it_does: Builds a forest of random-projection trees over fixed-length vectors and answers queries for the n closest items by vector or by existing item ID. Supports Euclidean, Manhattan, cosine (angular), Hamming, and dot-product distances. Indexes are built once, saved to a file, and loaded via mmap so multiple processes can share the same data with minimal memory. Query accuracy versus speed is tuned with n_trees at build time and search_k at query time. It also offers an on-disk build mode, distance lookups between items, and retrieval of stored vectors. The README also lists a C++ usage path via a single header include.
use_cases: find similar users or items from embedding vectors
music or product recommendation candidate search
nearest neighbor lookup over high-dimensional vectors
sharing a read-only search index across many processes
low-memory vector similarity search over large datasets
distributing prebuilt index files to production or batch jobs
how_to_run: from annoy import AnnoyIndex; t = AnnoyIndex(f, 'angular')
notable: Indexes are static files that are mmapped, so many processes can share one index with fast load
Small index memory footprint, a core design goal
Tunable trade-off via n_trees (build time) and search_k (query time)
Hamming distance packs data into 64-bit integers and uses bit-count primitives
Community bindings for R, Java, Scala, Ruby, Go, Lua, Node, Rust
caveats: Index is read-only after build or save; no more items can be added
Integer item IDs only, and memory is allocated for max(id)+1 items
Works better with fewer dimensions, per the README
Approximate results, not exact nearest neighbors
